messages:
logan: Heads-up: nightly kernel-harness picked up a perf regression for candidate kernel 'qkv-fused-v2' on Ampere when seqlen=512 + batch_path=adaptive. perf-ci flagged ~12% p99 increase. run id nightly/212350 - attaching quick logs.

devin: Ugh. Is this the case where KV cache fallback was triggered? I saw similar noise last month.

logan: Not exactly - logs show KV cache hits remain high. The interesting bit is the batching decision: when batch_path=adaptive we switch from continuous-batch to prefix-aware batching at seq 256->512 boundary and that picks a different kernel variant.

nathan: Can you paste the harness command and the minimal repro?

logan: Sure:```bash
./kernel-harness --arch ampere --kernel qkv-fused-v2 --seqlen 512 --batch_path adaptive --kv_cache enabled --runs 100 --measure p99
```
Output snippet:```
[INFO] run_id=nightly/212350
[RESULT] qkv-fused-v2 p50=1.2ms p95=3.6ms p99=6.8ms (baseline p99=6.1ms)
[PROFILE] kernel_variant=kv-aware-fused idx=3 oc=64
```

adia: If the chosen variant is kv-aware-fused idx=3 that might have an AVX alignment shim that regresses on Ampere memory stride. We saw a small penalty when batch sizes cross 16->32.

devin: Can we re-run with microprobe counters enabled and also pin batch to 16 to see if the kernel itself or the batch selection is the issue?

logan: Re-run scheduled:```bash
./kernel-harness --arch ampere --kernel qkv-fused-v2 --seqlen 512 --batch_path adaptive --kv_cache enabled --batch_max 16 --microprobe true --runs 200
```
Queued as nightly/212350-rerun-1.

perf-bot: perf-ci: rerun started (nightly/212350-rerun-1). Expect results in ~45m.

nathan: Also add the small test to unit microbench so CI picks it up: seqlen=512, batch=32, kv_cache=true, variant=kv-aware-fused. Put as flaky-tolerant for now.

adia: +1. I'll open a quick PR with the harness case and a label to skip on h100 for cross-arch isolation.

logan: Quick triage note: candidate gating rule currently allows up to 10% p99 delta for nightly sweeps before auto-hold. This one is ~12% so it tripped gating. We should probably make the gate aware of batch_path transitions rather than raw seqlen.

devin: Agreed. Short-term: add the microbench and pin the candidate to avoid rollout. Long-term: make autotuner consider sequence-length histograms and batch-aligned buckets.

nathan: I can prototype a fix to the autotuner policy: instead of single threshold per seqlen, evaluate kernel variants across (seqlen bucket, batch_size bucket, kv_cache flag). That will increase sample space but should reduce false positives.

logan: Action items: 1) add microbench test (adia) 2) block candidate rollout (devops) 3) autotuner proposal draft (nathan) 4) follow-up on perf-ci rerun (logan). I'll update the nightly ticket.

devin: FYI the rerun results are in — p99 delta dropped to 3% when batch_max=16, microprobe shows higher L1 TLB misses for batch=32 path.

logan: Good find. Sounds like a batch-alignment cache effect. Nate — that supports the batch bucket idea.

nathan: Yep. I'll start a small experiment to cluster input distributions and map them to kernel picks.

adia: PR opened: #3421 adding the seqlen=512/batch=32 kv-aware-fused microbench with skip-on-h100.

logan: Thanks. Leaving this thread open until autotuner PR lands. :thumbsup:
